reasons: Lake identity gives case_name_full as Kaupp v. Texas, court as U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 2003-05-05, and year 2003.
Lake citations list official 538 U.S. 626, parallel citations 123 S. Ct. 1843 and 155 L. Ed. 2d 814, and vendor-neutral 2003 U.S. LEXIS 3670.
The opinion frames and applies the Fourth Amendment seizure test, stating that Kaupp was arrested within the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.
The holding centers on whether police removal and station-house questioning constituted an arrest requiring probable cause, so Seizure of the Person is supported as a key home.
residual_risks: Role labels are partly corpus-taxonomic, but the disclosed text supports the substantive placement.

reasons: The opinion states Kaupp was advised of rights under Miranda before interrogation.

The opinion further discusses Brown's rule that Miranda warnings alone cannot always break the Fourth Amendment causal connection between an illegal arrest and confession, supporting a related cross-doctrine Miranda placement.
residual_risks: This is not a primary Miranda custody holding; the related cross-doctrine role avoids overclaiming.

reasons: The opinion begins by saying the case turns on the rule that a confession obtained by exploitation of an illegal arrest may not be used.
The opinion applies Wong Sun and Brown attenuation principles, assigning the State the burden to show purgation of taint.
residual_risks: The page body's Appears on section lists The Exclusionary Rule rather than Fruits & Attenuation, but the inventory/frontmatter home is substantively supported.

reasons: The text supports the facts: officers woke the 17-year-old at about 3 a.m., handcuffed him, took him from home to a patrol car, then to the crime scene and sheriff's headquarters for questioning.
The text states Kaupp's Okay was no showing of consent and no more than submission to lawful authority under the circumstances.
The text states the State did not claim probable cause and that suppression is required unless the confession was an act of free will sufficient to purge the taint, with the burden on the State.
residual_risks: The holding is compressed, but it tracks the opinion's limited remand posture by including the unless-taint-purged qualifier.
